[Thinking]
**Crafting statements and backstory**

I need to create 100 statements a client might say, focusing on detailed backstories but without any therapy advice. First, I should develop a concise backstory. I'm envisioning a 32-year-old woman who works as a software project manager, has gone through a breakup, and is an immigrant facing family expectations. Once I set up this background, I can number the statements to reflect that distinct and specific narrative. I'll keep it brief but impactful!
[/Thinking]

Here’s a brief backstory, then 100 distinct things this client might say.

**Backstory (for context only)**  
The client is **Alex**, a 32-year-old software project manager living in Boston. They immigrated from Brazil at 14. Their parents run a small cleaning business; Alex is the “successful one” in the family and sends them money monthly. Alex recently went through a painful breakup after a 6-year relationship with their partner, Maya, ended when Maya said Alex was “emotionally unavailable” and “always at work.” Alex has been struggling with depression and anxiety for years, with worsening symptoms over the last six months: insomnia, intrusive worries, panic-like episodes, trouble concentrating, and a persistent feeling of emptiness and pointlessness. They drink more than before—“just to take the edge off”—and have been missing deadlines at work, which is very unlike them. They also feel caught between cultures and guilty that they’re never doing enough for their parents or for themselves. They have been seeing this psychiatrist for several months.

---

### 100 things Alex might say in session

1. “I woke up this morning and my first thought was, ‘I can’t do another day of this.’ Not in a suicidal way exactly, just… exhausted by existing.”

2. “My boss sent another ‘we need to chat about your performance’ email, and my heart started racing so fast I thought I’d pass out.”

3. “You know those emails I never answer? Sometimes I open them 10 times, reread them, and then just close my laptop because I can’t make myself respond.”

4. “The breakup has been six months, but it still feels like it happened last week. I keep replaying the moment she said, ‘I can’t do this anymore’ like a movie in my head.”

5. “Maya said I was ‘never really present,’ and that keeps echoing in my head whenever I zone out with anyone now.”

6. “I’m scared that if I let myself really feel everything, I’ll just fall apart and won’t be able to put myself back together.”

7. “I know logically that other people love me, but it doesn’t feel true. It feels like they just tolerate me.”

8. “I feel guilty every time I send money to my parents because I resent it, and then I feel guilty for resenting it.”

9. “My mom keeps saying, ‘You’re so lucky to have such a good job,’ and I just nod, but inside I’m screaming because I hate going there.”

10. “Sometimes I think if my visa had never gone through and we’d stayed in Brazil, my parents would’ve been happier. They built their whole life around this American dream for me, and I’m miserable.”

11. “I keep canceling plans with friends and saying I’m ‘busy with work,’ but really I just don’t have the energy to pretend I’m okay.”

12. “I’ve been drinking more than I want to admit. It starts as one glass of wine to ‘relax’ after work, and then suddenly it’s the third glass and I’m still wired.”

13. “The meds make me feel… dull. Like the sharpest edges of the anxiety are gone, which is good, but so is some of the motivation.”

14. “I don’t know who I am outside of being ‘the responsible one’ or ‘the successful immigrant child.’ Without that, I feel empty.”

15. “I lie when people ask how I’m doing. I say, ‘Just tired,’ but it’s more like I’m tired in my bones, in my brain, in my soul.”

16. “I dread Sundays because I know Monday is coming. It’s like there’s a countdown in my head.”

17. “I avoid calling my parents because I don’t want to hear that edge in their voice, like they’re disappointed I’m still single and not giving them grandkids.”

18. “Honestly, I feel like I failed at the one ‘normal’ adult thing I was supposed to do—have a stable relationship—and now everything else feels pointless.”

19. “Sometimes I get this wave of panic at night where my chest tightens and I’m convinced something terrible is about to happen, even if I’m just in bed.”

20. “I’ve started sleeping with my phone under my pillow. I wake up every few hours and check it, even though nobody is texting me.”

21. “I know I should exercise, eat better, all of that, but even brushing my teeth sometimes feels like climbing a mountain.”

22. “There’s this constant voice in my head saying, ‘You’re not doing enough. You’re letting everyone down.’ And I can’t shut it off.”

23. “I scroll Instagram and see people from high school getting married, buying houses, having kids, and I just feel like I missed the train.”

24. “I tried meditation like you suggested, but sitting alone with my thoughts for five minutes felt unbearable. They just got louder.”

25. “On good days, I can almost pretend I’m okay, but it feels fake—like I’m wearing a costume.”

26. “I’m scared to tell my dad I’m in therapy. He still says things like, ‘Depression is for people who don’t work hard.’”

27. “When I was a kid, I translated everything for my parents—doctor’s appointments, bank meetings, immigration forms. Now when I struggle to send one email, I feel weak.”

28. “If I’m not constantly productive, I feel like I don’t deserve to exist. Rest feels like I’m stealing time I haven’t earned.”

29. “Sometimes I purposely work late just so I don’t have to go home to my empty apartment.”

30. “When I walk into the office, I feel like everyone can tell I’m faking it and they’re just waiting for me to mess up.”

31. “I’ve started having these thoughts like, ‘If I got hit by a bus, at least I wouldn’t have to go to work tomorrow,’ and that scares me.”

32. “Sleep is weird. I’m exhausted all the time, but when I lie down my brain starts replaying every awkward thing I’ve said since I was ten.”

33. “The last few panic attacks, I really thought I was having a heart attack. My hands went numb. I almost went to the ER but felt stupid.”

34. “I know we’ve talked about self-compassion, but when I try to say something kind to myself, it feels fake and embarrassing.”

35. “When Maya moved her stuff out, I told myself, ‘This is a chance to start over,’ but I haven’t started anything. I just sit in the same spot on the couch every night.”

36. “I caught myself rereading old texts from her at 2 a.m.—like maybe I’d find the exact moment I ruined everything.”

37. “At work, if someone gives me the slightest criticism, it confirms the story in my head: ‘You’re incompetent. They’re going to fire you.’”

38. “I feel like I’m carrying my family’s sacrifices on my back, and if I fall, it means their whole journey here was a waste.”

39. “I’ve been canceling these appointments in my head all week, and the only reason I showed up is because I felt guilty about wasting your time.”

40. “Some mornings I sit in the shower for 30 minutes because I can’t decide what to do first. Toothpaste or clothes becomes this impossible decision.”

41. “Whenever someone says ‘You’re so strong,’ I want to scream, ‘No, I’m just good at hiding how messed up I am.’”

42. “I feel like a fraud. Everyone thinks I’m this high-functioning professional, but they don’t see me staring at the wall at 3 a.m.”

43. “I get irrationally angry at little things—like when someone cuts in line—and then I hate myself for overreacting.”

44. “It’s hard to imagine a future that doesn’t feel like this. I can’t picture being genuinely excited about anything again.”

45. “I keep thinking, ‘If I were better—less needy, less anxious—maybe she would’ve stayed.’”

46. “Some days I don’t even recognize myself. I used to be social, funny, the one organizing trips, and now I’m… this.”

47. “I replay conversations after they happen, dissecting every word, convinced I said something wrong or sounded stupid.”

48. “Being in my body feels uncomfortable, like my skin is too tight or I’m buzzing with static.”

49. “I’ve started avoiding mirrors because I don’t like the person looking back. Not just looks—just… the whole person.”

50. “I’m afraid if I open up too much, you’ll think I’m overdramatic, like I’m making a big deal out of nothing.”

51. “I don’t want to scare you, but there are moments when I think, ‘If I just disappeared, it wouldn’t matter to anyone.’”

52. “At the same time, I’m terrified of dying. Even the thought of not existing sends me into a spiral.”

53. “It feels like I’m living someone else’s life, like I accidentally took a wrong turn at 22 and never got back on track.”

54. “I keep thinking I should be grateful. I have a job, I’m healthy, I’m in a safe country. Other people have it so much worse—who am I to be this depressed?”

55. “When my parents talk about friends back home who are struggling, they always add, ‘See how blessed you are?’ and I feel like I’m failing my blessings.”

56. “Sometimes I fantasize about quitting my job, moving somewhere nobody knows me, and starting over—but I know I’d just bring my brain with me.”

57. “I feel like my whole identity is built on achievements. If I’m not achieving, who am I?”

58. “I’m scared to slow down because I’m worried all the sadness I’ve been running from will catch up and drown me.”

59. “I don’t remember the last time I felt genuinely happy without alcohol or distraction.”

60. “When I try to remember good childhood memories, all I think about is translating scary letters from immigration lawyers to my parents.”

61. “There’s this pressure to be the ‘good immigrant story’—went to college, got a good job, made it. There’s no room in that story for depression.”

62. “I keep thinking I should’ve seen the breakup coming, but I was so focused on work that I missed all the signs.”

63. “I know self-harm isn’t the answer, but there are moments when emotional pain feels so intense that I just want some other kind of pain to drown it out.”

64. “I avoid starting big tasks because I’m afraid of failing, but then procrastinating makes me feel even worse. It’s this endless loop.”

65. “I feel like I’m constantly on the verge of tears, but if I start crying I’m afraid I won’t be able to stop.”

66. “Sometimes during meetings, I completely zone out and then panic because I have no idea what anyone just said.”

67. “I blame myself for everything—if someone is upset, I automatically assume it’s my fault, even if it obviously isn’t.”

68. “I feel like I have to perform different versions of myself for different people—‘American Alex’ at work, ‘Brazilian Alex’ at home, and I don’t know which is real.”

69. “When you ask how I’m feeling, my mind goes blank. It’s like I don’t have words for it—just this heavy fog.”

70. “I get this tight knot in my stomach on Sunday nights, and it just sits there until Wednesday.”

71. “I’m ashamed to admit how much time I spend just lying on the couch scrolling TikTok because it keeps me from thinking too much.”

72. “It embarrasses me that at 32, I still care so much about what my parents think, but I do. Their approval is like oxygen.”

73. “I feel jealous of people who can call their parents and say, ‘I’m not okay,’ and be met with support. I don’t have that.”

74. “When we talk about possibly increasing the meds, part of me feels relieved and part of me feels like that means I’ve failed at handling this on my own.”

75. “I hate how dependent I feel on weekly sessions with you. If we miss a week, I feel unmoored.”

76. “I’m worried if I get better, I’ll lose whatever edge made me good at my job. Like my anxiety is the thing that keeps me on top of everything.”

77. “There are days when the idea of showering, making food, answering messages—it all just feels like too much.”

78. “I know I push people away, then I get upset that they’re not closer to me. It’s like I’m sabotaging my own relationships.”

79. “When I look ahead five years, it’s just… blank. I can’t imagine anything good happening, but I also can’t imagine anything specific happening at all.”

80. “In meetings, if someone looks at me while I’m talking, I feel like I can hear my heartbeat in my ears. I just want to disappear.”

81. “Sometimes I pretend to laugh at work jokes I don’t find funny just so people won’t ask if I’m okay.”

82. “My friends keep saying, ‘You just need to get back out there and date,’ and I want to yell, ‘I can barely feed myself, I’m not ready to date.’”

83. “I feel like I’m wasting your time because other people probably have ‘real’ problems, not just being sad all the time.”

84. “When you ask me what I want, I genuinely don’t know. I’ve spent so long doing what I’m supposed to that I don’t know what I actually like.”

85. “I miss the version of me that could get excited about a weekend trip or a new restaurant. Now everything feels like a chore.”

86. “I’m scared to tell my friends how bad it is because I don’t want to be ‘the depressed one’ in the group.”

87. “If I’m not constantly available for my parents, I feel like a bad daughter, but being available all the time drains me.”

88. “Some nights, I lie in bed and mentally go through every mistake I’ve made in the last decade, like a playlist on repeat.”

89. “I’ve started writing notes in my phone when I feel really low, but when I reread them later, I feel embarrassed by how dramatic I sound.”

90. “I feel like my brain is split—one part knows these thoughts are irrational, and the other part is completely convinced they’re true.”

91. “I worry that if I let anyone see how anxious and depressed I really am, they’ll leave. Just like Maya did.”

92. “When you ask what I need, all I can think is: I want the noise in my head to stop, just for a little while.”

93. “I’m tired of every decision feeling like it has catastrophic consequences. Even small things feel like life or death.”

94. “I feel like I’m running a marathon on a treadmill—exhausted, sweating, but not actually going anywhere.”

95. “I keep telling myself, ‘Other people get through this, you should be able to too,’ and when I can’t, I feel like a failure at even being depressed.”

96. “I wish I could believe you when you say things can get better. It’s not that I don’t trust you; it’s that I don’t trust my brain to let it happen.”

97. “Sometimes I think the only reason I keep going is because I don’t want to hurt my family. If it were just about me, I don’t know what I’d do.”

98. “I don’t want to live like this forever, but I also don’t know how to live any other way. This has become my normal.”

99. “I’m scared that if I get better, I won’t recognize myself, and if I stay like this, I’ll lose myself completely.”

100. “What I want more than anything is to wake up one day and not have my first thought be, ‘How am I going to make it through today?’”
